react-virtualized is a set of React components for efficiently rendering large lists and tabular data.

 [!TIP]
 If you're considering adding react-virtualized to a project, take a look at react-window as a possible lighter-weight alternative.

 Support

Most of react-virtualized's styles are functional (e.g. position, size) and are applied directly to DOM elements.
The Table component also ships with a few optional presentational styles; to use them, import the CSS file once (e.g. while bootstrapping your application):

 

The package is marked as side-effect free (other than its CSS), so bundlers will tree-shake any components you don't use.

 TypeScript types

TypeScript definitions are included within the published dist folder.
Types are exported for each component's props (e.g. ListProps , GridProps , TableProps ) along with the parameters passed to renderers (e.g. RowRendererParams , CellRendererParams , TableCellProps ).

 Pure components

By default all react-virtualized components are wrapped in memo to avoid re-rendering unless props or state has changed.
This occasionally confuses users when a collection's data changes (eg ['a','b','c'] = ['d','e','f'] ) but props do not (eg array.length ).

The solution to this is to let react-virtualized know that something external has changed.
This can be done a couple of different ways.

 Pass-thru props

This shallow comparison will detect changes to any props, even ones a component doesn't use.
This means you can also pass through additional properties that affect cell rendering to ensure changes are detected.
For example, if you're using List to render a list of items that may be re-sorted after initial render- react-virtualized would not normally detect the sort operation because none of the properties it deals with change.
However you can pass through the additional sort property to trigger a re-render.

 Public methods

 Grid components can be forcefully re-rendered by calling forceUpdate on their ref.
For Table and List , you'll need to call forceUpdateGrid to ensure that the inner Grid is also updated. For MultiGrid , you'll need to call forceUpdateGrids to ensure that the inner Grid s are updated.

 Documentation

Documentation and live examples for every component are available at react-virtualized-docs.vercel.app, along with how-to guides for things like sizing components, infinite loading and server rendering.

 [!NOTE]
 AutoSizer is no longer part of react-virtualized (as of version 10); it is available as the separate react-virtualized-auto-sizer package.

 

 Components

 ArrowKeyStepper

This HOC decorates a virtualized component and responds to arrow-key events by scrolling one row or column at a time.
This provides a snap-to behavior rather than the default browser scrolling behavior.

Note that unlike the other HOCs in react-virtualized, ArrowKeyStepper adds a element around its children in order to attach a key-down event handler.
The appearance of this wrapper element can be customized using the className property.

 Required props

 
 
 
 Name 
 Description 
 
 
 
 
 children 
 Function responsible for rendering children.
It is passed onSectionRendered and registerChild parameters, which should be attached to the decorated
virtualized component (e.g. <Grid onSectionRendered={onSectionRendered} ref={registerChild} /> ),
and the scrollToColumn and scrollToRow indices of the active cell (e.g. to highlight it).
The active cell is scrolled into view through the registered component& 39;s scrollToCell method. 
 
 
 
 columnCount 
 Number of columns in grid; for Table and List this property should always be 1 . 
 
 
 
 rowCount 
 Number of rows in grid. 
 
 
 
 

 Optional props

 
 
 
 Name 
 Description 
 
 
 
 
 className 
 CSS class name to attach to the wrapper <div> . 
 
 
 
 disabled 
 Disables all scrolling using arrow-keys. 
 
 
 
 isControlled 
 This component is "controlled"; it will not update scrollToColumn or scrollToRow itself.
This property should be used with onScrollToChange . 
 
 
 
 mode 
 Controls behavior of stepper when arrow key direction changes.
"cells" means that the index will only increment or decrement by 1;
"edges" means that the opposite side of the grid will be incremented. 
 
 
 
 onScrollToChange 
 Called when arrow key navigation should update the current scroll-to values. 
 
 
 
 scrollToColumn 
 Default/initial scrollToColumn value.
When isControlled is true, this is the current scrollToColumn value. 
 
 
 
 scrollToRow 
 Default/initial scrollToRow value.
When isControlled is true, this is the current scrollToRow value. 
 
 
 
 

 CellMeasurer

Wraps a cell and measures its rendered content.
Measurements are stored in a per-cell cache.
Cached-content is not be re-measured.

The child must be a DOM element (e.g. ) or a component that passes its ref along to one;
otherwise use a function child and pass registerChild as the ref of the element to be measured.

 Required props

 
 
 
 Name 
 Description 
 
 
 
 
 cache 
 Cache to be shared between CellMeasurer and its parent Grid .
Typically an instance of CellMeasurerCache . 
 
 
 
 children 
 Either a React element as a child (eg <div /> ) or a function
(eg. ({ measure, registerChild }) => <div ref={registerChild} /> ). 
 CellMeasurer attaches a ref to the child element to find the DOM element to measure
(the child& 39;s own ref , if any, still receives the element).
